THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Chitradurga, judgment and award dated 10.04.2017 in MVC No.266/2016.
2.
The factum of accident and injuries sustained are not in dispute in this case.

3. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.
4.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
4.1 The claimant has sustained injury in road accident that occurred on 24.04.2010 at about 9.30 p.m., when the claimant and others were traveling in lorry NC:
2024:KHC:20807 bearing reg.No.KA-28-A-2715 from Nalluru to Hiriyuru and said lorry was dashed to another lorry bearing reg.No.MH- 09-BC-4292 as head on collusion.
Therefore, the claimant sustained injuries.
5. The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act., claiming compensation before the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.1,23,000/- with interest at 9% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed before this Court.

6. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:

sentences.text: As per the doctors evidence the claimant has suffered 9% of permanent disability found to be correct considering to the nature of injury sustained, accident is caused in the year 2010, therefore, notional income Rs.5,500/- is for consideration.
The claimant was 15 years old was working as barber helping his father.

Therefore,
Rs.5,500/- is considered as notional income.

NC: 2024:KHC:20807 Therefore, 'loss of future income due to disability' is hereby reassessed and quantified as under:
Rs.5,500 X 9% X 18 X 12 = Rs.1,06,920/-
Thus, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,06,920/- under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.

Towards 'loss of amenities', is awarded as Rs.25,000/- as against of Rs.20,000/-
Towards food, nourishment and attended charges etc., is of Rs.10,000/-.
8.

Thus in all the claimant is entitled to compensation as under:

In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,02,420/- as against Rs.1,23,000/- as mentioned in the table above.
10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,23,000/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,02,420/-.
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,02,420/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
